title: Spring Security: authentication, authorisation and JWT

videos.script: Until now, anybody could place an order in the bookshop, in anybody's name. {{open}} The order said who the customer was, and the server believed it. This lesson ends that. {{chain}} Spring Security puts a chain of filters in front of every controller. A request that cannot say who it is stops there, with a 401. A request that may not do what it asks stops there too, with a 403. {{passwords}} The bookshop has two users, and it never keeps their passwords. It keeps bcrypt hashes, which are slow to compute on purpose. {{token}} So a password is checked once, and buys a token. The token is a JWT: three parts, signed with a secret only the server holds. You will decode one and see that anybody can read it. Then you will change one word in it, and watch the server refuse it. {{scopes}} The token carries scopes. Ana may place orders. Only the clerk may add a book. {{orders}} And an order now belongs to whoever's token placed it. Ask for somebody else's, and the bookshop answers that it does not exist. {{end}}
